image.subject: a bare winter field at dawn, a blackened wooden stake standing in a low bed of grey ash, thin smoke drifting across the frozen ground, no people

storyboard.claim: The execution was chosen to erase who the victims were, not to deliver justice.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a bare winter field at dawn, a blackened stake in grey ash, thin smoke, no people
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the point that a burning in a hanging era means a deliberate cover-up.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fire destroys the body, and with it the proof of who died.

image.subject: a man in his forties, neat build, short hair, tweed jacket, polite but intense, leaning across a small retro diner table toward a woman in her thirties, slim build, shoulder-length dark hair, plain modern clothes, tired expression, two cheeseburgers on plates between them

storyboard.claim: Henry is the expert who explains the hidden dynamic to Julia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry leaning across a diner table toward Julia, two cheeseburgers between them
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts from the abstract cover-up to the people who will explain it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Henry is the curator, and the setting is a casual diner, not the museum.

storyboard.claim: Henry is casually offering Julia historical gossip over lunch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a light banter beat with no picture
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Stays on the diner table and marks the tone shift to chatty history.
storyboard.addedInformation: Henry frames the next revelation as gossip, not evidence.

image.subject: an old yellowed court record lying open on a wooden library table, dark brown ink handwriting that cannot be read, a pair of reading glasses resting beside it, a single lamp

storyboard.claim: Henry has studied the Wood Haven trials in depth and knows the real accuser.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a yellowed 1692 court record on a library table with reading glasses beside it
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Backs the claim with the expertise Henry just mentioned.
storyboard.addedInformation: The primary accuser was not a hysterical girl as in Salem, and the record shows it.

storyboard.claim: The surprising name is Molly, a servant, not a teenager.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a question card with no picture
storyboard.onScreenText: THE PRIMARY ACCUSER WAS A WOMAN NAMED MOLLY
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Julia's question sets up the answer that Molly is the accuser.
storyboard.addedInformation: The accuser was a servant, which changes the whole story.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, plain build, brown hair under a cap, rough servant's dress, standing before a wooden bench in a dim 1692 meeting house, hands folded, eyes lowered

storyboard.claim: Molly was a poor servant who testified that Caroline was a witch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Molly in a rough servant's dress and cap, hands folded, before a wooden bench in a dim meeting house
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives Molly a face after her name was asked.
storyboard.addedInformation: Molly is a poor household servant in the Eldridge home.

image.subject: a cold village field at dusk, a low grey mound of ash and a charred stake, a cart standing empty at the edge of the trees, no people

storyboard.claim: Caroline is executed and reduced to ash, and the ash is the end of her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a cold field at dusk, a grey mound of ash and a charred stake, empty of people
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the outcome of the testimony, not the act itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: Caroline's body is destroyed, so no one can later prove who was burned.

left.label: SERVANTS' QUARTERS
left.subject: a small bare attic room with a narrow cot, one candle on a plank table, plain wooden walls, no people

right.label: MASTER BEDROOM
right.subject: an empty canopy bed with heavy dark curtains in a candlelit timber room, no people

storyboard.claim: Molly rises from the servants' quarters into the master bedroom after marrying Archie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a split: a bare servants' attic on the left, a grand four-poster bedroom on the right
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The marriage moves Molly from the bottom of the house to the top.
storyboard.addedInformation: Molly takes the mistress's room in the same house.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, plain build, brown hair under a cap, rough servant's dress, standing at a tall gilt mirror in a candlelit bedroom, wearing a dark period gown that is too fine for her

storyboard.claim: The servant literally takes the mistress's place in the household.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Molly in a servant's dress before a gilt mirror, wearing a dark gown that is too fine for her
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the replacement the compare beat only described.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mistress's gown on the servant makes the swap visible.

image.subject: a woman in her seventies, composed, grey-streaked hair, cardigan, cold expression, standing in a dim doorway of an old timber house holding a heavy flashlight

storyboard.claim: Celia takes Ethel's place, repeating the 1692 pattern in the present day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Celia in a cardigan in a dim doorway, holding a heavy flashlight
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the modern servant into the frame as the mirror of Molly.
storyboard.addedInformation: Celia is the present-day replacement, not the original mistress.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house at night under a low moon, a dark turned-over garden plot in front of it, no people

storyboard.claim: The house lets the poor take the place of the rich, as long as the land is fed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a timber house at night with a dark freshly turned garden plot in front
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the people to the house that repeats the pattern.
storyboard.addedInformation: Peton itself is the force that rewards the cycle.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, plain build, brown hair under a cap, rough servant's dress, a faint sly half-smile, standing at the edge of a crowded 1692 village square, townspeople gathered behind her looking up at a meeting house

storyboard.claim: Molly stirred the town's witch panic to win a rich husband and an estate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Molly with a sly half-smile at the edge of a crowded village square
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ties Molly's personal ambition to the wider hysteria.
storyboard.addedInformation: Molly is the one who drove the accusations, not a bystander.

storyboard.claim: Molly is a calculating mastermind, and the book's answer lands on her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a punchline card with no picture
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the Molly theory with one blunt line.
storyboard.addedInformation: Molly is praised as a villain, which the next beat will undercut.

image.subject: a wooden chess board mid-game in candlelight, one white pawn knocked over beside a dark king, no hands

storyboard.claim: Molly was a pawn in a much larger game.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a chess board with a knocked-over pawn beside a dark king
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Overturns the mastermind theory with a visual metaphor.
storyboard.addedInformation: There is a larger player behind the accusations.

image.subject: an old bound ledger page open on a wooden desk, a candle beside it, brown ink lines too faded to read, a dated 1717 heading in the page margin, no people

storyboard.claim: The real answer is in the 1717 epilogue.
storyboard.concreteVisual: an old ledger page on a desk with a candle, faded ink lines, no people
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shifts the search from 1692 to the later record.
storyboard.addedInformation: The true monster appears twenty-five years later in the record.

image.subject: a young woman in her twenties, slim, long pale hair under a plain linen cap, dark period dress, frightened eyes, standing close beside a hulking man with wild dark hair in a shadowed stone prison doorway, a guard's lantern in the background

storyboard.claim: Caroline and Jonas Reev were lovers, and neither was executed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Caroline and a hulking man with wild dark hair close together in a shadowed prison doorway
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Reveals the relationship the 1692 story hid.
storyboard.addedInformation: Caroline and the supposed killer were lovers, which reverses the accusation.

image.subject: a stone jailhouse yard at night, a leather coin purse passed through a wooden gate to a guard holding a lantern, two shadowy figures slipping away into the dark

storyboard.claim: The lovers bribed their way out and fled the colony.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a leather coin purse passed to a guard at a gate, two figures slipping away into dark
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the escape the narration just stated.
storyboard.addedInformation: The escape was paid for, which is the first sign of the family's money.

image.subject: a seventeenth-century timber house at night under a thin moon, two dim figures on the cobbled lane in front of it, faces not visible

storyboard.claim: Twenty-five years later, the two return to Peton in the dead of night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a timber house at night with two dim figures on the lane, faces not visible
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the escape to the homecoming.
storyboard.addedInformation: The return to Peton is planned, not accidental.

image.subject: a rough servant's dress and a plain linen cap laid across a bed beside a dark period gown, candlelight on the cloth, like costumes set out for a play

storyboard.claim: Caroline and Jonas steal the identities of Molly and Archie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a servant's dress and cap laid across a bed beside a dark gown, candlelit
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the costume of the impersonation that the narration describes.
storyboard.addedInformation: The identity theft is set up with costumes, not a person.

image.subject: a man in his fifties, heavy build, dark wool coat, white collar, stern face, standing in a wood-panelled hall of a timber manor, a lit candelabra beside him

storyboard.claim: Jonas steps into Archie's life as the wealthy merchant.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a heavy man in a dark wool coat and white collar in a wood-panelled hall
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the impostor in Archie's place.
storyboard.addedInformation: The impostor wears Archie's coat and collar, so he looks like the husband.

storyboard.claim: The layers of identity theft are too much to follow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a punchline card with no picture
storyboard.relationToPrevious: A reaction to the impostor reveal.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond the reaction itself.

storyboard.claim: Caroline returns decades later, kills her husband and the servant, then lives as the woman who accused her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a question card with no picture
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the chain of events in one sentence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Caroline is the one who kills her husband and the servant.

image.subject: a small oval hand mirror on a dark wooden table, reflecting a young woman's face in a plain linen cap, a candle beside it

storyboard.claim: Caroline wears the face of her enemy to sleep in her own bed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: an oval hand mirror reflecting a young woman in a plain linen cap beside a candle
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the disguise the recap just described.
storyboard.addedInformation: The face in the mirror is the one she took from the woman who accused her.

storyboard.claim: The identity theft is layered and deliberate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a reaction card with no picture
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Confirms the recap in one line.
storyboard.addedInformation: None beyond confirmation.

image.subject: a timber manor house in grey dawn light, its heavy chestnut front door standing open onto a dim hall, no people

storyboard.claim: The house keeps and absorbs these false identities.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a grey dawn view of a timber manor with its heavy front door open onto a dim hall
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the people to the house that welcomes them.
storyboard.addedInformation: The house is shown as an open door, not as a jailer.

image.subject: a heavy chestnut front door of a timber manor standing wide open at night, warm candlelight spilling onto the flagstones, no people

storyboard.claim: Peton welcomes false identities as long as the cycle continues.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a wide-open chestnut door with candlelight on the flagstones, no people
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Repeats the house image with a warmer, inviting light.
storyboard.addedInformation: The house takes the parasites in, not out.

storyboard.claim: The Wood Haven Museum is the modern force digging up the buried past.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a place card with no picture
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the modern threat into the story after the house.
storyboard.addedInformation: The museum is the present-day institution uncovering the history.

image.subject: an empty brick museum gallery with a glass case under soft light, no people

storyboard.claim: Henry walks Julia through the museum to pitch her on buying the house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Henry gesturing at a glass case beside Julia inside a brick museum gallery
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts Henry and Julia in the museum for the sales pitch.
storyboard.addedInformation: Henry wants to buy the house, which the museum tour is meant to win.

image.subject: red brick facade of a historic building in daylight, clipped hedges, empty front lawn, no people

storyboard.claim: The museum is a clean, controlled brick castle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a red brick museum with clipped hedges and a manicured lawn, daylight, no people
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the pitch to the building itself.
storyboard.addedInformation: The brick building is shown as a sterile fortress for the past.

image.subject: a colonial spinning wheel, a heavy ornate wooden chest and two silver candlesticks on display in a dim glass-cased museum room, no people

storyboard.claim: The museum holds the period objects that Henry wants to display.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a spinning wheel, a carved chest and silver candlesticks behind museum glass
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Shows the artifacts the narration lists.
storyboard.addedInformation: The objects are sterile museum pieces, separated from the house they came from.

left.label: THE MUSEUM
left.subject: period artifacts behind glass in a clean museum room, a spinning wheel, a carved chest and silver candlesticks, no people

right.label: PETON
right.subject: the seventeenth-century timber house Peton at dusk, its windows dark, no people

storyboard.claim: Henry wants to move the museum's sterile artifacts into the real house.
storyboard.concreteVisual: a split: museum artifacts behind glass on the left, the dark timber house at dusk on the right
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the museum display with the house Henry wants.
storyboard.addedInformation: Henry plans to buy the house and put the artifacts inside it.

storyboard.claim: Henry wants a authentic portal to colonial times for tourists, which sterilizes horror.
storyboard.concreteVisual: none, a statement card with no picture
storyboard.onScreenText: A PORTAL TO COLONIAL TIMES FOR TOURISTS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the pitch with Henry's stated plan.
storyboard.addedInformation: The plan turns the horror of the past into a tourist attraction.
